Photograph: Mark Schiefelbein/AP Trump administration Federal agents search Ilhan Omar’s home as part of fraud investigation Video posted by Fox shows what appears to be law enforcement in HSI jackets at Omar’s DC residence Matt Shuham Mon 12 Oct 2026 09.46 EDT First published on Mon 12 Oct 2026 08.50 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Federal agents searched Representative Ilhan Omar’s home Monday morning as part of a criminal investigation, according to the department of justice and reports in the Associated Press and Fox News. A video posted by Fox showed what appeared to be law enforcement in HSI jackets at what Fox News said was Omar’s Washington DC residence. “Today in the Washington, DC area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice. This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation,” a DoJ spokesperson told the Guardian. It was unclear what the nature of the warrant was – neither Omar’s office, DoJ, the department of homeland security nor the White House immediately responded to the Guardian’s requests for comment. Fox News reported based on unnamed sources familiar with the matter that agents were examining the immigration paperwork that the congresswoman’s father filled out when she was a child. Donald Trump and key allies have accused Omar of fraud related to her family’s immigration history, fantasizing openly about denaturalizing her and expelling her from the country. The congresswoman has consistently denied the accusations, though Trump has repeatedly made them national news with gratuitous attacks against Omar, who along with Representative Rashida Tlaib became the United States’s first Muslim congresswoman in 2019. But even amid a presidency known for political and legal retribution against his critics, the search of Omar’s DC home just three weeks before a crucial midterm Election Day will surely lead to new accusations that Trump was using the government for his own political ends. Administration officials, and the president himself, have long hinted at a federal investigation into Omar. “Let’s see what happens,” Trump said at a rally on Saturday after attacking Omar by name, adding that Vice-President JD Vance “and our people are looking at it very strongly”. It was just the latest in months of talk about investigating Omar. Trump in December accused her of having “married her brother” and said she “should be thrown the hell out of our country”, a reference to a years-old but unsubstantiated claim that Omar sought to help her ex-husband – who they allege is really her brother – obtain immigration papers via a sham marriage. Days later, his “border czar” Tom Homan said : “We’re pulling the records now,” referring to Omar, and said a fraud investigator in Homeland Security Investigations, the ICE division that historically has been tasked with investigative work, would look into the matter. In March , Vance told rightwing media personality Benny Johnson: “We actually think that Ilhan Omar definitely committed immigration fraud” and that he had recently spoken to top Trump aide Stephen Miller about “what the remedies are”. Homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin told Johnson last month that there was an ongoing investigation and “something’s going to happen”. “We know that she married her brother to try to bring him into the United States,” Mullin said. “We know he lives now in London. We feel that there may be more to this, the whole family migration, and possibly some illegal activity for them to come to the United States to begin with. But all of us, we’re investigating.” Soon after, Homan said he could not “comment on an ongoing criminal investigation. “We’ll let HSI, Homeland Security Investigations continue to do their investigation,” he added. Omar has for years denied unsubstantiated rumors from Trump and others about herself and her family, including the accusation that her ex-husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, is in fact her brother, and that the marriage was part of an effort to earn him immigration status. Marriage fraud is a felony, though it has a five-year statute of limitations. Omar and Elmi formally divorced in 2017 after separating in a religious divorce years earlier. The New York Post last month also quoted an unnamed “top immigration official” who said “the Trump administration could initiate a denaturalization process” against Omar if there is sufficient evidence that she or her father lied on immigration applications. The story noted accusations that Omar was older than her recorded age of 17 when she was naturalized, which could be relevant because she received citizenship via her parents. The report also raised questions about Omar’s father, who reportedly claimed to be an educator, though his obituary later described a military career. As the most prominent Somali-American in the United States, Omar has faced years of racist attacks from the president and his supporters. At his rally Saturday, Trump said of Somalia: “All they have is crime and squalor” and suggested that “our” US constitution did not belong to Omar. Two days earlier, he had written that Minnesota “is being taken over by Somali Immigrants”, even though the vast majority of Somali-Americans in the state are US citizens. “The Somalians should not be allowed to get away with what they are doing,” Trump wrote, urging supporters in the state to “fight back!” Somali-Americans, especially, have borne relentless insult from the White House in Trump’s second term. In December, the president referred to them as “ garbage ” who “come from hell, and they complain, and do nothing but bitch”. “Let them go back to where they came from and fix it,” he added. https://www.walesonline.co.uk/whats-on/s.text: Beauty advent calendars are not only a beloved way to count down to Christmas Day, but also a brilliant opportunity to revamp skincare routines at a fraction of the cost of buying products individually. One brand, loved by Alison Hammond, has now unveiled its own calendar, offering shoppers savings of nearly £370 on gentle yet indulgent formulas. Tropic Skincare has launched its 24 Days Of Pure Imagination advent calendar , packed with a remarkable 27 products valued at £668. Priced at £299, shoppers save £369 on the contents, which include a carefully curated mix of skincare, body care, makeup, fragrance and wellbeing treats. Founded in 2004 by 15-year-old Susie Ma, who began selling her handmade body scrubs at London's Greenwich Market, Tropic caught the eye of Lord Alan Sugar when the young entrepreneur appeared on The Apprentice in 2011. He later invested in the brand before Susie bought out Lord Sugar to become sole CEO in 2023. READ MORE: Light sleepers snap up £30 off blackout silk mask like 'luxury spa experience' 'I had weekly blow drys but £40 hair tool gives same result in 10 minutes at home' The British beauty brand has gone from strength to strength, recently welcoming This Morning favourite Alison Hammond as a brand ambassador, The Liverpool Echo reports. A beautician at her hair salon first introduced the 51-year-old to the brand, and she has been a devoted fan ever since. In an Instagram video, Alison recently showcased Tropic's Radiance Cleanser, saying: "We're going to start with a radiance cleanser. Look how good this is; it literally melts off my makeup. I've got really dry skin, so I absolutely love this. She added: "No pain whatsoever. Literally coming off in one cleanse. I'm using Tropic which is a beautiful brand." The very same Radiance Cleanser Pore-Refining Cleansing Oil features in the advent calendar as a 30ml miniature, making it an ideal size to try before committing. Normally £36 for 95ml, it works out to about £11 as part of the calendar. Formulated to deliver a clearer, softer and more radiant complexion, the cleanser harnesses the power of vitamin C. At the same time, azelaic acid helps reduce inflammation, refine pores, and even out skin tone. One satisfied shopper remarked on the product: "Absolutely amazing cleanser! It leaves my skin feeling so clean, fresh, and soft without making it feel dry or tight. I've also noticed that it's helping to minimise the appearance of my pores, and my skin looks smoother and more refined." Another enthusiastic reviewer added: "Absolutely love using this. It's worked wonders on my face, especially on my problem areas like my forehead and nose. Pores are less visible, and skin feels great. It also smells really nice as well." One customer did, however, deduct a star, noting that it occasionally 'struggles to remove my mascara first cleanse', though they acknowledged it did 'make my skin feel so smooth and soft'. For those seeking an alternative, the well-regarded Lipid-Balance Cleansing Oil from Medik8 ( £35 ) is worth considering. Containing Moringa extract and Safflower Oil for a luxuriously silky texture, it deeply nourishes the skin while strengthening the skin barrier. Meanwhile, Pai Skincare stocks this Light Work Cleansing Oil ( £34 ). Enriched with omega-rich rosehip oil, the formula nourishes and cleanses at once, leaving skin feeling soft, luminous and revitalised. Returning to Tropic , the cleanser is far from the only standout product in the countdown. Among the full-size offerings are the Glow Berry Brightening Serum, Rainforest Dew Hydration Serum, Sun Day Dewy Facial SPF 50, Eye Lift Exosome Midnight Balm and Youth Potion Enriched Retinal Complex, the last of which carries a value of £78 on its own. Rounding out the collection are the Body Smooth Refreshing Polish, Hand Therapy Softening Superfood Cream, Foot Remedy Softening Buttercream and Lashful Eyelash Growth Serum. For those who love fragrance and cosmetics, there are also a Bergamot Peel and Crushed Leaf Eau de Parfum and an All Eyes On You Face and Body Liquid Highlighter. Perhaps the most exciting inclusion, however, is the Lamellar Milk Barrier Repair Essence, a brand-new product exclusive to the calendar. Advent calendar purchasers will get to try it ahead of its official launch, which isn't scheduled until 2027. The calendar not only grants shoppers an exclusive first look at the product, but also delivers a carefully curated selection of the brand's best-loved formulas at a fraction of their usual cost - ideal for refreshing your skincare regimen or as luxurious stocking fillers and gifts for loved ones.
